note: Chat link spans and card eligibility. Offsets are UTF-16 code units, half-open. `url` is the resolved URL (https:// prepended when the match had no scheme). `card` is null or the first card-eligible Flipcash link in the message, with its jump wrapper already unwrapped. A match whose following character is non-ASCII is rejected. Behavior parity, not a computation with an external reference.

vectors.name: bare-cash-link
vectors.note: The shape the bug report screenshot showed: nothing but the link.

vectors.name: text-around-link
vectors.note: Card above, this whole string as the caption beneath it.

vectors.name: two-links-one-card
vectors.note: Both links are tappable spans; the first card-eligible one wins.

vectors.name: bare-domain
vectors.note: No scheme: still a link, resolved with https://. A reserved path, so no card.

vectors.name: app-host-cash-link
vectors.note: Both hosts and both path spellings reach the same route.

vectors.name: jump-wrapped-cash-link
vectors.note: The card's url is the unwrapped target; resolution needs that, not the redirector.

vectors.name: glued-emoji-host
vectors.note: No span at all. The trailing character is non-ASCII, so the match is rejected: iOS by authorityIsASCII, Android by the boundary rule.

vectors.name: lookalike-host
vectors.note: A link, because it is one. Not a card: the host is not in cardHosts, and both route classifiers match on path alone, so nothing else would have stopped it.

vectors.name: login-link
vectors.note: Carries the account seed. Never a card, whatever the host says.

vectors.name: verify-link
vectors.note: Carries a verification secret. Never a card.

vectors.name: tip-card-by-id
vectors.note: Card-eligible per the spec, but not in phase 1 (open decision 4). Span only.

vectors.name: token-link
vectors.note: A token link renders as that token's bill. The mint is taken from the path and is not validated here -- an unknown mint is a card that never resolves, not a rejected one.
